hero.name: Ananya
hero.who: a 23-year-old customer support executive in Indore who worries about every opinion

story.b: Ananya's day starts with a fight. The auto driver near Rajwada asks for twenty rupees extra, and she argues with him for ten minutes. At the office, her team lead walks past without saying good morning, and she spends an hour wondering what she did wrong. The canteen poha is cold. Her Sunday dance reel has only forty-one views, and she checks it nine times before lunch. Then her colleague Mansi says her kurta is very bright, and Ananya replays that line all afternoon. On the bus home at seven, she feels completely drained. Her brother calls to ask about her bank exam preparation. She has not opened the book in two weeks, and she cannot explain where all her energy went.

ask.q: Ananya ends each day exhausted but cannot name one thing she did for herself. What is the most useful first step?
o: Notice where her worry goes for a day and ask which of it really matters
Force herself to stop worrying through sheer willpower
Post more reels so the low views stop bothering her
ask.why: Ananya cannot choose what to care about until she sees where her care is going. Willpower alone turns worrying into worrying about worrying. Chasing more views feeds the same drain. A simple look at her day shows how much energy goes to things that will not matter next week.

chapters.take: Before you fix your worries, notice where your care is going.

story.b: That Sunday, Ananya sits on the terrace with a cup of chai and her old college notebook. On one page she writes what truly matters to her: her health, her parents, her friend Kavya and the bank exam. On the next page she writes three things she will stop caring about this week: reel views, auto fare fights and Mansi's remarks about her clothes. On Monday the auto driver asks for extra again. She pays, puts in her earphones and listens to a current affairs podcast. Her team lead looks grumpy, and she reminds herself that his mood belongs to him. At lunch she solves twenty reasoning questions instead of checking her phone. By Friday she feels oddly light.

ask.q: On Friday, Mansi makes another comment, this time about Ananya's dupatta. What should Ananya do?
o: Plan a sharp reply for Monday so Mansi finally stops
Ask three other colleagues whether the dupatta really looks bad
Smile, let it pass, and spend her lunch break on exam practice
ask.why: A comment about a dupatta is not on Ananya's short list of what matters. Planning a comeback or collecting opinions spends the very care she is trying to save. Letting it pass and using the time for her exam puts her energy exactly where she chose to put it.

chapters.take: Saying no to small worries is how you say yes to big ones.

story.b: Kavya is applying to a fashion design course, and she happily stays up till two sketching. Ananya admires that. She wants the bank job badly, or she thinks she does: a steady salary, a proper desk, her parents proud at family weddings. But every morning the alarm rings at six for mock tests, and she hates it. Her scores are low. Sunday outings are gone. One evening she asks herself a different question. Not what she wants, but which daily struggle she is willing to live with. The honest answer surprises her. She does not mind early mornings, and she secretly enjoys cracking reasoning puzzles. What she hates is the fear of failing in front of relatives.

ask.q: Ananya likes the idea of a bank job but dreads the daily grind. Which question will help her most?
o: Which job would make my relatives most proud?
Which daily struggle am I actually willing to live with?
Which path promises me the least stress?
ask.why: Every goal comes with its own kind of pain. Relatives' pride will not get her through boring mock tests at six in the morning, and no path is free of stress. Asking which struggle she can accept shows Ananya what she truly values, and gives her a reason to keep going.

chapters.take: Ask not only what you want, but which struggle you will accept for it.

story.b: In March, Ananya clears the first stage of the exam. She celebrates with her parents over pani puri at Chappan Dukan and expects to finally relax. Two days later the next problem arrives. The main exam syllabus is twice as long, and her company moves her to the evening shift. For one night she sulks and tells Kavya that life never lets her breathe. Then she looks at her old list of worries, the reel views and the auto fares, and compares them with this one. This problem is hers. She chose it, and it is taking her somewhere. She turns her bus rides into study time, asks her manager for two morning shifts a week, and gets back to work.

ask.q: Ananya clears one stage and immediately faces a harder one. How should she see this?
o: As a better problem, one she chose and is glad to work on
As proof that life is unfair and she can never relax
As a sign she should quit before things get worse
ask.why: Problems never stop, they just change shape. Calling the new stage unfair, or quitting, treats problems as something to escape. Seeing it as a better problem, tied to her own goal, lets Ananya put her energy into solving it instead of resenting it.

chapters.take: Life is never problem free. Choose problems you are glad to have.

story.b: A customer complains loudly about a wrong policy update, and the blame lands on Ananya. The real mistake was made by Sunil, a senior on the next desk, who keyed in the wrong date. Her monthly review drops a grade. For two evenings Ananya is furious. She rehearses angry speeches on the bus and misses her study hours. On the third evening she sits down and separates two things. The mistake was not her fault. But how she responds is her responsibility. She pulls up the call times and system notes and sends her manager a short, calm email. She also starts writing a one-line note after every call, so her work is always on record. Then she opens her books again.

ask.q: A senior's error has cost Ananya a good review. What is her best response?
o: Tell everyone in the office about Sunil until they see the truth
Accept it silently, since nothing can be done anyway
Share the call records calmly, keep her own notes, and move on
ask.why: The mistake is not Ananya's fault, but her response is her responsibility. Venting to everyone keeps her stuck in anger and can backfire. Staying silent gives away her power. Calmly sharing the facts and tightening her own process puts her back in charge of what happens next.

chapters.take: It may not be your fault, but your response is still yours.

story.b: Since Class 8, when she forgot her lines in a school play, Ananya has been sure she freezes in front of groups. So when her manager asks her to train two new joiners for an hour, her first answer is almost no. That night she asks herself a strange question. What if this belief is wrong? What if it was just one bad afternoon ten years ago? The next day she says yes. She makes a page of notes and walks into the small training room with sweaty palms. She loses her place twice and laughs it off. The joiners ask good questions, and one of them thanks her later on the team chat. Ananya writes down one lesson: bigger notes, fewer slides.

ask.q: Kavya is sure she is bad at presenting her designs, and an interview asks her to present. What should Ananya tell her?
o: Skip it, since she already knows presenting is not her thing
Try it, even clumsily, and treat any stumble as useful information
Wait until she has done a full public speaking course
ask.why: A belief built on a few bad moments is not proof. Skipping protects the belief instead of testing it, and waiting to feel ready can take years. Trying, even clumsily, gives Kavya real information, and the stumbles show her exactly what to work on next.

chapters.take: Hold your beliefs about yourself loosely. Some of them are simply wrong.

story.b: Ananya still takes the same auto from Rajwada, and some days the driver still asks for extra. Some days she pays, some days she smiles and says no, and either way she forgets it by the office gate. Mansi still has opinions about her clothes. Ananya now finds them funny. She trains every new batch of joiners and keeps her notes in a blue folder. The main exam is done and the result is weeks away, but she sleeps well. She still posts dance reels for fun and checks them once, maybe twice. When Kavya asks how she stopped worrying, Ananya says she did not stop. She just worries about far fewer things, and only ones that matter.

chapters.take: Calm does not come from caring less, but from caring about the right few things.
